title: Only Even Rolls
statement: You roll a fair die until you get a $6$. Given that every roll you made was even, what is the expected number of rolls?
insight: The condition really means 'stop at the first roll in {1,3,5,6} and keep only runs that stopped on 6'. The stopping time is independent of which value it stopped on.
redHerring: Answering 3 by pretending the die only has faces 2, 4, 6.
hints: Conditioning is not the same as changing the die to {2,4,6}. Which runs are being thrown away?
A run survives exactly when the first roll in $\{1,3,5,6\}$ is a 6.
Is the time of the first roll in $\{1,3,5,6\}$ independent of which of those four values it is?
solution:
Consider the first roll landing in $S=\{1,3,5,6\}$. The run is kept exactly when that roll is 6. The number of rolls $T$ until hitting $S$ is geometric with $p = \tfrac46$, and the value at $T$ is uniform on $S$ independently of $T$.

So conditioning on "the value was 6" does not change $T$'s distribution: $E[T] = \tfrac64 = \tfrac32$.
